In
this
paper,
we
conducted
a
preliminary
study
on
the
development
of
a
digital
therapeutic
for
rehabilitation
using
motion
recognition
technology
based
on
Google's
Teachable
Machine
to
analyze
exercise
postures
and
provide
real
-
time
feedback
.
The
developed
system
is
expected
to
enhance
rehabilitation
efficiency
by
reducing
subjectivity
in
movement
execution

.
1

screen

rehabilitation
exercise
in
progress
along
with
the
ROC
curve
.
The
sensitivity
of
the
ROC
curve
was
defined
as
the
proportion
of
correctly
recognized
side
lunge
motions
among
all
actual
side
lunge
attempts
by
the
participant
.
Specificity
was
defined
as
the
proportion
of
correctly
identified
non
-
side
lunge
motions
among
all
instances
where
the
participant
did
not
perform
a
side
lunge
.
For
each
of
the
n
participants,
sensitivity
and
1
-
specificity
values
were
calculated
.
These
values
were
then
sorted
in
descending
order
of
sensitivity
and
ascending
order
of
1
-
specificity
for
ROC
curve
representation
.
The
recognized
rehabilitation
movements
are
computed
through
machine
learning,
requiring
the
subject
to
perform
the
exercises
accurately
.
Consequently,
this
approach
is
expected
to
enhance
the
efficiency
of
rehabilitation
.

•
The
application
was
developed
using
Visual
Studio
Code
and
implemented
with
HTML,
JavaScript,
and
CSS
for
the
user
interface
.
It
was
designed
to
be
accessible
on
both
PC
and
mobile
devices
in
a
web
environment,
with
an
intuitive
design
to
ensure
ease
of
use
.
•
Motion
recognition
functionality
was
implemented
using
Google's
Teachable
Machine
.
This
system
was
trained
to
recognize
specific
movements
required
for
anterior
cruciate
ligament
rehabilitation
exercises,
enabling
posture
analysis
.
The
motion
recognition
algorithm
classifies
four
stages
of
rehabilitation
exercises
and
determines
whether
the
user's
movements
are
correct,
allowing
for
counting
and
feedback
provision
.
•
To
provide
real
-
time
voice
feedback
when
users
perform
incorrect
postures
or
complete
specific
movements,
Naver
Clova
AI's
speech
recognition
and
synthesis
API
was
integrated
.
This
feature
enables
users
to
receive
voice
feedback
and
correct
their
posture
in
real
time
.
The
final
web
application
was
designed
for
deployment
on
the
Netlify
platform
for
easy
accessibility
and
distribution
.
•
To
evaluate
the
effectiveness
of
the
developed
digital
therapeutic,
an
experiment
was
conducted
with
32
healthy
adults
aged
20
to
24
.
Participants
performed
20
repetitions
of
the
side
lunge
exercise,
during
which
the
program
recorded
the
number
of
correctly
recognized
and
unrecognized
movements
.
Based
on
the
collected
data,
sensitivity
and
specificity
were
calculated,
and
an
ROC
(Receiver
Operating
Characteristic)
curve
was
generated
using
Microsoft
Excel
to
assess
the
model's
performance
.
Methods
•
The
growing
importance
of
treating
and
rehabilitating
physical
injuries,
as
well
as
the
need
for
ongoing
rehabilitation
exercises
after
surgery
to
prevent
recurrence
and
aid
recovery,
is
increasingly
emphasized
due
to
the
aging
population
and
the
rising
interest
in
sports
activities
[
1
-
2
]
.
Digital
therapeutic
devices
are
defined
as
evidence
-
based
therapeutic
interventions
driven
by
software
to
prevent,
manage,
or
treat
medical
disorders
or
diseases
.
These
devices
are
characterized
by
their
ability
to
provide
treatment
and
management
using
universal
hardware,
such
as
smartphones,
to
enhance
accessibility
and
serve
many
people
at
a
relatively
low
social
cost
.
•
In
this
paper,
we
conducted
a
preliminary
study
on
the
development
of
a
digital
therapeutic
for
rehabilitation
using
motion
recognition
technology
based
on
Google's
Teachable
Machine
•
The
digital
therapeutic
system
we
developed
for
rehabilitation
exercises
accurately
recognizes
the
user's
movements
and
posture
.
It
displays
the
number
of
completed
repetitions
on
the
screen
and
provides
voice
feedback
on
posture
in
real
time
.
Additionally,
by
using
the
membership
registration
and
login
features,
users
can
track
their
individual
exercise
progress
.
•
Rehabilitation
exercises
using
this
system
are
expected
to
guide
users
in
performing
precise
movements,
reducing
the
subjectivity
of
physical
therapists'
assessments
and
improving
treatment
efficiency
.
